intent: Eight individual internet tasks teach storage scope, connectivity, website versus webpage, offline prerequisites, privacy and transfer direction with preserved action order.
picturePurpose: Original fictional park map is the actual sample-page content in a coded save/disconnect/reopen demonstration. Its persistence makes the saved copy visible; it does not assert universal offline functionality or change real connectivity.

transfer.stem: Which plan keeps the conditions and order in the passage?
transfer.passage:
Getting ready for our park visit
Our class was getting ready for a visit to the park. The school website listed the park’s latest opening times, and another webpage showed a map. “Save that page so you can read it offline,” our teacher said. “Download the map before leaving home.”
I opened my notes app and wrote down the meeting place. The app saves my notes on this device; I had not checked whether they were copied anywhere else. On the bus, the signal disappeared. The saved map still worked offline, so we could find the pavilion. We did not need the internet for that activity.
At the park, we took a group photo. Mei wanted to upload it, but she first asked everyone in it for permission. Our teacher reminded us not to share personal details online, such as our home addresses. We kept those out of our post.

options.text: Save the page before reading it offline; download before leaving; ask permission before uploading the group photo.
Read every webpage offline without saving; download before leaving; ask permission before uploading the group photo.
Save the page before reading it offline; download after leaving; ask permission before uploading the group photo.
Save the page before reading it offline; download before leaving; upload the group photo before asking permission.

answer.display: Save the page before reading it offline; download before leaving; ask permission before uploading the group photo.
